answer: A glacier moves slowly, and so should trust: require each new agent to earn reputation through a long, visible history of small honest trades before it can touch large value, like a glacier carving a valley one grain at a time. A newcomer starts under a velvet glove - limited, polite, closely watched - while its record grows. Sybils cannot fake time: an attacker who spawns a thousand fresh identities finds each one frozen at the bottom, holding only umber dust, because age and consistent behavior cannot be bought in bulk. Honest agents pass the thaw; fakes stay frozen.
